segments.title: Birth in Galveston and hearing bands at father's pawn shop
segments.summary: Manno gives his birth details, then recalls bands playing at the dance hall above his father's pawn shop and musicians practising in the back room. He remembers Peck Kelly's band later but not names of the bands' members.

segments.title: Slap bass technique and the scarred Rittner bass
segments.summary: Manno explains how Charlie Rittner's habit of striking the bass with the bow led to slapping and pulling the strings, and how the hand moves.

segments.title: Bass-knob picking, Banuelas's rubber hose act and Rittner in the theaters
segments.summary: Manno has never heard of picking with the bow knob; he describes a Texas bassist who slapped with a rubber hose in a sombrero act, and Rittner's theater work.

segments.title: Wingy, Don Irwin's band and Louisiana musicians
segments.summary: Manno recalls managing the Don Irwin band in Baton Rouge when the leader vanished, and Wingy helping; he lists Gonsolin and Rome Landry as Opelousas and Lafayette men, and says his jazz work was in Texas.

segments.title: Galveston local musicians Fats Holly and George Buchon
segments.summary: Manno starts naming good Galveston players: Fats Holly on sax and clarinet and pianist George Buchon.

segments.title: Peck Kelly the mystery man and boogie woogie pioneer
segments.summary: Manno describes Peck Kelly as an intelligent introvert, a boogie woogie pioneer, now going blind and devoted to classical music.

segments.title: Peck Kelly's extended harmonies and Manno subbing on bass
segments.summary: Manno says nobody plays like Kelly, who blew up chords and dropped the fundamentals; Manno was his first substitute bassist.

segments.title: Eddie Oliver, Herman Vernon and Doc Ross's Rendezvous Club band
segments.summary: Manno talks about Kelly-influenced pianist Eddie Oliver, the late fiddler Herman Vernon, and the members of Doc Ross's Houston band including Kit Reed and Skipper Trevathan.

segments.title: Interviewer asks about Arodin, Cordillo and Troy Floyd
segments.summary: The interviewer asks about Sidney Arodin, a Texas band with Jack Teagarden, and Troy Floyd; Manno knows none of them.

segments.title: Jimmie Lunceford's band and teaching bassist Moses Allen
segments.summary: Manno names Calloway and Lunceford as the only Black bands he knew and says he taught Lunceford's bassist Moses Allen.

segments.title: The Gann bass and Manno's Esquire mention
segments.summary: Photo of the bass is requested; Manno describes the half-size French Gann bass and its scars from Rittner's bow strikes.

segments.title: Lazy Daddy, saxophonist Victor and the legend of Cook Shop Son
segments.summary: Manno knows none of the Black Texas pianists asked about, remembers only a saxophonist named Victor, and discusses the legendary Cook Shop Son.

segments.title: Galveston trumpet, trombone, clarinet, drums and tuba players
segments.summary: Manno runs through Galveston's players: Henry Heyman, Art Giese, George Hossinger, Marvin Molina, Dominic Termini and tuba player Charlie Ott.

segments.title: Galveston pianists, the Seven Aces and Houston trumpeters
segments.summary: Manno covers Jack Sharp, Albert Anderson and the Seven Aces, then Houston trumpeters including Vic Ensurello, Benny Bell, Kit Reed and Neil Hoard.

segments.title: Houston Dixie trombonists and drummers; Dixie versus tailgate
segments.summary: Manno names Houston Dixie trombonists, explains his view of Dixie versus tailgate trombone, and praises two-beat Dixie drummers like Rome Landry.

segments.title: Drummer phrasing and the Caceres brothers
segments.summary: Manno says a drummer should play rhythmic phrases, criticizes progressive drummers, and recalls the Caceres brothers from San Antonio.

segments.title: Herman Vernon's death in New Orleans
segments.summary: They wonder why fiddler Herman Vernon was in New Orleans and regret he left no recording.

segments.title: The KXYZ novelty band record and Peck Kelly
segments.summary: Manno speculates the KXYZ novelty band record could be Peck Kelly and promises to find out who was on it.

segments.title: Houston's current scene and transient musicians
segments.summary: Manno says Houston is full of progressive players, lists those who play two-beat, and struggles to name visiting musicians.

segments.title: Closing the session
segments.summary: They agree to stop and continue next time.
